about.title: El Segundo Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: El Segundo residents rely on nearby South Bay and Los Angeles County medical facilities for everything from routine care to emergency treatment, and most of the time that care goes as expected. But when a provider misses a diagnosis, makes a surgical error, or mismanages a medication, the harm can be lasting and hard to sort through on your own. California law places specific limits on these claims, including a short window to act and a required 90-day notice before a lawsuit can even be filed. A qualified medical expert almost always has to review the case before it moves forward, since a poor result by itself doesn't establish that a provider did anything wrong. We handle medical malpractice claims in El Segundo and can review your medical records, timeline, and what actually happened to explain your options in plain terms.

whyChoose.title: Why El Segundo Residents Choose Us

items.title: You're Not Alone With the Clock
items.desc: California generally gives you one year from when you discover the harm, and no more than three years from the injury itself, to bring a claim. We can help you figure out exactly where you stand before that window closes.

items.title: The 90-Day Notice Requirement Is Handled Correctly
items.desc: Before a malpractice lawsuit can even be filed in California, the provider must receive a 90-day pre-suit notice. Getting this step right matters, and our team knows how to prepare it properly.

items.title: Understanding the Non-Economic Damages Cap
items.desc: California's MICRA law caps non-economic damages, though that cap rises each year by statute. We can walk you through how that cap may apply to your specific situation, and what a qualified medical expert's review might show.

items.question: How long do I have to file a medical malpractice claim in El Segundo?
items.answer: California generally requires you to file within one year of discovering the injury, and no more than three years from the date it occurred, whichever comes first. There are some exceptions, so it's worth having us review your specific timeline. Waiting too long can permanently close off your ability to bring a claim.

items.question: Does a bad medical outcome automatically mean malpractice happened?
items.answer: No. California law is clear that a poor result alone does not prove negligence occurred. A claim typically requires showing the provider fell below an accepted standard of care, which is why a qualified medical expert almost always has to review the records first.

items.question: I live in El Segundo but was treated at a hospital outside the city. Does that matter?
items.answer: Not usually. What matters is where the care was provided and the facts of what happened during treatment, not your home address. Our team can look at where the treatment occurred and guide you on next steps regardless of which facility was involved.
